title: Building this website
lead: A running record of how this site is built and what changes as I work on it.
body: This is a living post about the site itself, so it doubles as a changelog. I update it whenever the site changes.
A note on AI assistance

The code behind this site was built with the help of an AI assistant, and I want to be upfront about that. The ideas, the decisions, and the reviews were mine: what the site should do, how it should look and read, and what to include or leave out all came from me, and I checked every change as it went in.

The writing is a clearer line. Every project write-up, the resume, the experience notes, and everything else on this site are written entirely by me. The only two pieces that involve AI are the ones about the site itself — this blog post and the "This Website" project card. Everything else is my own words.
A static site, on purpose

This is a plain static site: hand-written HTML and CSS with a little vanilla JavaScript — no frameworks and no build step. It is hosted for free on GitHub Pages and served at derekhan.link. There are no accounts, no analytics, and no tracking.
Content lives in data files

Every page reads its text from a small JSON file under data/, and one script (assets/js/render.js) fills the HTML using simple data-bind and data-list attributes. That means updating the site is editing JSON, not markup — while the structure and styling stay in HTML templates and CSS.
Fast to load, sharp to look at

Images are stored in two sizes: a 1000px "display" copy for cards and sliders, and a 2560px "lightbox" copy that is fetched only when you click an image. When the lightbox opens it shows the small image instantly, then swaps in the sharp one. Every image is re-encoded with orientation baked in and its EXIF/GPS metadata stripped — which keeps the pages quick and the location data private. A script regenerates both tiers from the full-resolution originals kept outside this repo.
Contact me for original files.
Galleries, sliders, and a lightbox

Project pages show their photos as a horizontal slider, so the writing stays on screen, and any image opens in a lightbox with keyboard navigation. The project grid, the tag filter, and the ordering are all generated from data/projects.json.
The blog you are reading
This blog is JSON-driven too: each post is a file under data/blog/ plus a one-line entry in data/blog.json. To add a post, copy data/blog/_template.json. There is nothing more to configure.
Changelog
Everything that went into this site, newest first.
Latest
<ul>
• Awards and experience entries can now carry links (a row of buttons), and their text fields accept inline HTML links.
• Populated the Awards & Honors list and the Experience page (research, work, and extracurriculars) from my college-application activity lists.

• Images and YouTube videos can now be mixed: add a video entry to any project's media or the Gallery. It shows a poster with a play button, plays inline on project pages, and opens in the lightbox in the Gallery.
• Moved the Gallery link into the top navigation and removed it from the footer on every page.
• Added an AI-assistance note to this post and the "This Website" card, and started this changelog.
• Built the JSON-driven blog: posts live in data/blog/<slug>.json, are listed in data/blog.json, and render through post.html?slug=…. Added a reusable _template.json and a sample post.
• Images now load in two tiers — a 1000px display copy for cards and sliders, and a 2560px lightbox copy fetched only on click — and every image has its EXIF/GPS metadata stripped for privacy.
• Added Scripts/regenerate-images.py to rebuild both image tiers from the full-resolution originals kept outside the repo, preserving the SVG placeholder and banner.
• Optimized all photos for the web (much smaller files, faster pages).
• Project pages show their photos as a horizontal slider with a click-to-enlarge lightbox and optional captions.
• Fixed project ordering so the Home and Projects pages list projects in ID order (my ranking of importance).
• Added the "This Website" project card — a portfolio that catalogues itself.
Content & data
<ul>
• Moved all page text out of the HTML and into data/*.json, filled by a small renderer (render.js) using data-bind and data-list.
• Reformatted projects.json for legibility and split long descriptions into readable arrays of HTML blocks.
• Made the resume, experience, awards & skills, contact, and gallery pages fully data-driven.
• Project titles can include simple HTML (for example italic titles).
Design & features
<ul>
• Added a banner image to the Home hero while keeping the blueprint grid.
• Added a Gallery page for photos and artwork, linked discreetly in the footer.
• Dark mode, tag filtering, scroll animations, a responsive layout, and a collapsible mobile menu.
Foundations
<ul>
• Initial build: a plain static site — hand-written HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, no frameworks and no build step — with a technical/engineering visual design.
• Hosted for free on GitHub Pages and served at derekhan.link.
• Added robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and a favicon for search engines and link previews.
